// ── Knowledge Base ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export const KB = [
  { id:'ws-express', tags:['workspace','create','express','server','project'], title:'Creating a Workspace — CE Express',
    answer:`To create a workspace in CE Express:
1. Log in → click **Workspaces** tool in left toolbar
2. Click **New workspace**
3. Enter workspace name, EPSG coordinate system code (e.g. 32635 for UTM35N), and draw the extent on the map
4. Select your **Geodata set** (DEM + clutter)
5. Click **Save**

The map zooms to the workspace extent and only objects in this workspace will be visible.

→ See full docs: [Workspaces](#ce-express-workspace)` },

  { id:'ws-pro', tags:['workspace','create','pro','desktop','arcgis'], title:'Creating a Workspace — CE Desktop Pro',
    answer:`To create a workspace in CE Desktop (Pro):
1. Open ArcGIS Pro → CE toolbar → **Workspace Tool**
2. Click **Create Workspace**
3. Choose or create a File Geodatabase (.gdb)
4. Enter workspace name
5. Browse to your **geodata folder** (DEM, clutter, antennas)
6. Select **projected coordinate system** (UTM or national grid — NOT WGS84)
7. Click **Create**

⚠️ Always use a projected coordinate system — geographic (lat/lon) will give inaccurate distance calculations.

→ See full docs: [CE Pro Workspace](#ce-pro-workspace)` },

  { id:'rf-run', tags:['rf','prediction','run','coverage','how to','required'], title:'Running RF Prediction',
    answer:`To run RF Prediction in CE Express:
1. Select cells on the map (Features tool → Select)
2. Click **RF Prediction** in the left toolbar
3. Set: Prediction type (Coverage, Best Server, RSRP, SINR...), Resolution (50m recommended to start), Radius, Propagation model
4. Click **Run** → results appear as a raster layer

**Required inputs:**
- DEM/terrain raster covering the prediction area (mandatory)
- Antenna pattern (.msi or .pln) assigned to each cell (mandatory)
- Clutter/land-use raster (recommended)

→ Full guide: [RF Prediction](#ce-express-rf-prediction)` },

  { id:'rf-required', tags:['required','rf','prediction','what','need','inputs'], title:'What is Required to Run RF Prediction?',
    answer:`**Mandatory:**
- DEM (terrain elevation raster) covering the full prediction area
- Correct projection matching the workspace EPSG
- Antenna pattern (.msi or .pln) assigned to each cell
- At least one propagation model configured

**Strongly recommended:**
- Clutter/land-use raster (improves accuracy significantly)

**For urban / ray-tracing:**
- 3D building data (LoD1 height polygons or full 3D mesh)

→ Full guide: [RF Prediction](#ce-express-rf-prediction) | [Geodata Requirements](#geodata-requirements)` },

  { id:'prop-models', tags:['propagation','model','okumura','cost231','ray tracing','which'], title:'Propagation Models Available',
    answer:`CE Express/Pro includes these propagation models:

| Model | Frequency | Best For |
|-------|-----------|----------|
| Okumura-Hata | 150–1500 MHz | Rural/suburban macro |
| COST-231 Hata | Up to 2 GHz | Urban/suburban macro |
| COST-231 W-I | 800MHz–2GHz | Dense urban micro |
| SPM | Configurable | General, can be tuned |
| Ray Tracing 3D | Any | Highest accuracy, needs 3D buildings |
| CE Custom | Any | Tuned against drive-test data |

CE evaluates LOS/NLOS1/NLOS per pixel and applies the most appropriate model.

→ Full guide: [Prediction Models](#ce-express-prediction-models)` },

  { id:'install-pro', tags:['install','installation','activate','activation','ce pro','desktop','arcgis pro'], title:'Installing CE Desktop Pro',
    answer:`**Installation order (important!):**
1. Install **ArcGIS Pro** first (v2.8 or later)
2. Run **CE Desktop installer** as Administrator

**Activation:**
1. Open ArcGIS Pro → **Project → Settings → Licensing**
2. Enable the **CE Desktop** extension
3. A User Key is generated → send it to support@cellular-expert.com
4. You receive an activation file → apply it in License Manager

**For upgrades:** Uninstall old CE version first, then install new one.

→ Full guide: [Installation](#ce-pro-installation)` },

  { id:'install-express', tags:['install','express','server','admin','prerequisites'], title:'Installing CE Express (Server)',
    answer:`CE Express server requirements:
- Windows Server 2016/2019/2022 (or Ubuntu 20.04+)
- ArcGIS Server 10.9.1+
- PostgreSQL 13+ with PostGIS
- PHP 7.4+
- IIS (Windows) or Nginx (Linux)
- Min 16 GB RAM, 8 CPU cores, 500 GB storage

→ Full installation guide: [CE Express Installation](#ce-express-admin-installation)` },

  { id:'geodata', tags:['geodata','dem','terrain','clutter','data','format','requirements'], title:'Geodata Requirements',
    answer:`CE requires these GIS datasets:

**DEM/Terrain (mandatory):**
- Format: GeoTIFF (.tif) recommended
- Resolution: 5–30m (finer = more accurate but slower)
- Must use projected coordinate system (NOT WGS84 lat/lon)
- Must match workspace EPSG code

**Clutter/Land-use (recommended):**
- Same raster formats, 8-bit or 16-bit integer classification
- Categories: Open, Rural, Forest, Suburban, Urban, Dense Urban, Water

**Buildings (for urban/ray-tracing):**
- Vector polygons with height attribute (LoD1) or 3D mesh (LoD2)

→ Full guide: [Geodata Requirements](#geodata-requirements)` },

  { id:'import', tags:['import','csv','data','network','bulk','excel'], title:'Importing Network Data (CSV)',
    answer:`To import sites and cells from CSV:
1. Features tool → click **Import features**
2. Select object type (Site or Cell)
3. Drag & drop your CSV file
4. Use **Column Mapping** to match your column names to CE fields
5. Click **Import** — objects appear on map immediately

**Minimum CSV for cells:**
\`\`\`
CellName,Latitude,Longitude,Azimuth,Height,Technology
CELL001,51.5074,-0.1278,0,25,4G
\`\`\`

Supported formats: CSV, KMZ

→ Full guide: [Network Object Requirements](#network-object-requirements)` },

  { id:'license', tags:['license','activation','error','expired','key'], title:'License Issues',
    answer:`Common license issues and fixes:

**"License not found":**
- CE not activated → send User Key to support@cellular-expert.com
- License Manager → verify CE extension is enabled

**"License expired":**
- Contact sales for renewal: info@cellular-expert.com

**"License server unreachable" (floating license):**
- Check firewall: port 27000 TCP/UDP must be open between client and license server
- Ensure License Server service is running

**For offline activation:**
- Generate activation request file → send to support → apply response file

→ [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)` },

  { id:'los', tags:['line of sight','los','profile','terrain','fresnel'], title:'Line of Sight / Profile Analysis',
    answer:`To run a profile/LOS analysis in CE Express:
1. Click **Profile** tool in the left toolbar
2. Click **Draw Profile** → click two points on the map
3. Set frequency and K-factor (default 4/3 for standard atmosphere)
4. CE computes the terrain cross-section using the loaded DEM

**Result colours:**
- 🟢 Green = clear LOS
- 🟡 Yellow = marginal (Fresnel partially blocked)
- 🔴 Red = obstructed

For microwave links, the 1st Fresnel zone should be at least 60% clear.

→ Full guide: [Profile & LOS](#ce-express-profile)` },

  { id:'mw-link', tags:['microwave','mw','backhaul','radio link','point to point'], title:'Microwave / Radio Link Planning',
    answer:`To plan a microwave link in CE Express:
1. Select two sites on the map → right-click → **Create Link**
2. Set frequency (GHz), polarisation, assign antennas and radio model
3. Run **Profile** to check LOS and Fresnel zone clearance
4. Run **Link Prediction** → view RSL, fade margin, availability (%)

CE uses ITU-R P-series models for atmospheric absorption, rain fade, and multipath fading.

→ Full guide: [Radio Link Prediction](#ce-express-radio-link)` },
];

export function findAnswer(query) {
  const q = query.toLowerCase().trim();
  const words = q.split(/\s+/).filter(w => w.length > 2);
  let best = null, bestScore = 0;
  KB.forEach(item => {
    let score = 0;
    words.forEach(w => {
      if (item.title.toLowerCase().includes(w)) score += 6;
      item.tags.forEach(t => { if (t.includes(w) || w.includes(t)) score += 4; });
      if (item.answer.toLowerCase().includes(w)) score += 1;
    });
    if (score > bestScore) { bestScore = score; best = item; }
  });
  return bestScore >= 4 ? best : null;
}
